display-figure.purpose: The one stake figure per screen: gap to rival or total points. Condensed, red behind, blue ahead.

title.purpose: Screen titles, plate head, sheet heads (20px).

section-title.purpose: Below-fold section heads on the Plan screen.

gain-figure.purpose: Per-move gain and captain xPts on the plate, in armband yellow.

move.purpose: The Out → In line on each plate row; primary button text.

body.purpose: Running text and table cells; captions at 13px in ink-2.

counter-name.purpose: Player names under magnets, condensed, on a translucent board chip; tab labels at 11px.

label.purpose: Uppercase board markings and component labels only (Out lane, Subs, in order). Never an eyebrow above a headline.

marker.purpose: Board annotations only, rotated -4 to -6deg. Never the only carrier of a value.

shadows.name: magnet
shadows.purpose: A counter at rest on the board.

shadows.name: lift
shadows.purpose: A counter on hover or when its move is selected.

shadows.name: panel
shadows.purpose: Plate, subs strip, tables, active rail item.

shadows.name: frame
shadows.purpose: The aluminium frame hanging on the wall.

shadows.name: board-recess
shadows.purpose: The melamine set into the frame.

shadows.name: sheet
shadows.purpose: Bottom sheet on phones; side sheet uses -8px 0 30px rgb(21 24 28 / 0.16). Backdrop rgb(21 24 28 / 0.42).

shadows.name: primary
shadows.purpose: The team ID submit; the only coloured shadow. No hard offset lip.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Standard ease for lifts, sheets, chevrons and the arrow draw.

motion.name: counter-lift
motion.purpose: Magnet transform and shadow on hover and selection.

motion.name: arrow-draw
motion.purpose: Marker strokes drawing in on load and on re-solve (stroke-dashoffset 1 to 0).

motion.name: sheet-rise
motion.purpose: Sheet rises 24px (phone) or slides 32px (desktop) from 60% opacity.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Plate row hover background, primary button press and colour.

motion.name: dim
motion.purpose: Unselected arrows and gains fade to 28%; chevron rotation.

motion.name: breathe
motion.purpose: Loading ghost board and plate, opacity 0.55 to 1.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: animation and transition durations 0.01ms; arrows render fully drawn

narrative.overview:
Every working screen is a white melamine board in a brushed-aluminium frame, hung on a cool grey wall. The squad sits on it as glossy magnetic counters; the week's transfers are drawn in red marker, each arrow pulling an outgoing counter off the pitch to the incoming one. Beside the board hangs one dark plate that lists the same moves in type, with the evidence under each. The metaphor is literal enough to be read at a glance on a phone before the deadline, and the data never depends on it: everything on the board is said again, in set type, somewhere readable.

Density is a manager's, not an analyst's. One stake figure, one board, one plate, then the long tables below the fold for anyone who wants them. Type is a single workhorse grotesque (Archivo) whose width axis does the hierarchy work: condensed and heavy for figures and names, normal width for reading. Hand lettering (Permanent Marker) is the marker on the board and nothing else.

The system is light only, on purpose. A whiteboard is a light object, and the product is used on phones in daylight, on the bus or at work, in the days before a deadline. There is no dark theme and no `prefers-color-scheme` branch; the browser chrome is tinted to the wall (`themeColor` #E6E8EB). The one dark surface is the reversed plate, which is an object in the room, not a mode.
keyCharacteristics: Physical materials, rendered lightly: wall, framed board, magnets, marker. No textures, no photographs.
One grotesque on a width axis; condensed for numbers, normal for words; tabular figures everywhere.
Blue is yours, red is change, yellow is the captain and the gain. Each is always paired with a shape or letter.
One reversed plate and one display-scale figure per screen.
Marker annotates; type carries the data.
Motion is the marker being drawn and the magnet being lifted; nothing else moves on its own.

rules.name: The Magnet Meaning Rule
rules.body: Blue means a player you keep, red means a player arriving or leaving, yellow means the captain or a gain. Do not use these three for decoration, categories or charts.

rules.name: The Colour-Plus-Shape Rule
rules.body: Colour is never the only signal. Captain and vice carry the letters C and V; outgoing counters are a dashed ring with the name struck through; rival-owned players carry a letter disc; doubles carry "×2"; doubt carries its own badge; the stake figure carries "behind" or "ahead" in words beside it.

rules.name: The Width-Axis Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy for numbers comes from the width axis and weight, not from more faces. Any figure that is a name or a number on a counter, a gain, or the display figure is set condensed (`.cond`, width 72%).

rules.name: The Marker Annotates Rule
rules.body: Permanent Marker is never the only place a value appears. The board's marker gains are `aria-hidden` and repeat a figure the plate sets in type. Marker never sets labels, buttons, headings or body copy.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` is set on the body; columns of figures always align.

rules.name: The League-Column-Survives Rule
rules.body: On phones (below 760px) low-value table columns give way so the league columns survive: Bench and Price diff hide, and the Edge header drops its "vs Rival" tail, while League EO and Edge always stay visible.

rules.name: The Board-First Rule
rules.body: On every working screen the framed board is the largest object in the first viewport; tables and long copy live below it.

rules.name: The Lift-Means-Selected Rule
rules.body: A counter rises (translateY -3px, scale 1.07, lift shadow) only when you hover it or its move is selected. Outgoing ghosts never cast a shadow; a lifted ghost fills with red-soft instead.

dos: Do keep exactly one reversed plate (plate on plate-text) per screen; everything else sits on the wall or the board.
Do keep exactly one display-scale figure per viewport, condensed at width 72%, against small labels.
Do pair every magnet colour with a shape, letter or word: C and V, dashed ring plus strikethrough, the rival letter disc, "behind"/"ahead".
Do give everything drawn on the board a typed equivalent: the plate lists every move, the key explains every mark.
Do put each claim beside its proof: a move's stat line sits directly under it, a landing claim sits beside its demonstration.
Do keep player rows to the same fields in the same places across plate, sheet and tables.
Do use the standard ease (cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)) for lifts, sheets, chevrons and the arrow draw; 160 to 320ms for state, 640ms for the stroke.
Do honour reduced motion: all animations and transitions collapse to 0.01ms, arrows appear fully drawn, sheets appear in place, the loading ghost holds still.
donts: Don't add a dark theme or a `prefers-color-scheme` branch; the board is a light object used in daylight.
Don't set data, labels, buttons or headings in Permanent Marker, or let a marker figure be the only place a value appears.
Don't use blue, red or yellow for anything but their magnet meanings, and don't put yellow text on the board.
Don't add a second reversed plate, a second display figure, or a stack of stat cards; the board carries the screen.
Don't put an uppercase eyebrow above a headline; the 10px uppercase label is for board markings and component labels only.
Don't set the product name as a tracked-caps eyebrow above a heading; the wordmark is 17px 800 in sentence case on its own row.
Don't introduce a second grotesque or a separate display face; use Archivo's width axis.
Don't let anything animate on its own after the arrows are drawn, except the loading ghost.
